My own state, Alaska, for example, poured federal funds from the Connect America program into the local ISP monopoly - GCI Alaska - so that GCI could build out a new and robust network to connect rural Alaskans who don't have broadband access. Now I'm paying $160 a month for 6mbps and a 40GB monthly cap because GCI owns the network and has no reason not to bleed us dry with their monopoly.

What I wish the U.S. would do is take responsibility for its own infrastructure like it did with highways in the 1950s. Roll out publicly owned networks like it rolled out highways, and connect the rural areas that ISPs won't touch. Stimulate the economy by creating jobs with the construction of the network. Then open the network up for any size ISP to offer service over, charge a maintenance fee, and let any mom and pop ISP compete with the big guys. Dozens of ISPs competing on service instead of one or two gate guardians squatting on subsidized networks.
